name: Saint Camillus de Lellis
history: A soldier and gambler who lost everything, was converted while labouring for Capuchin friars, and gave the rest of his life to the sick. He founded the Ministers of the Sick, whose red cross later became a familiar sign of care for the wounded. He is the patron of the sick, of nurses and of hospitals.
life: Camillus was born at Bucchianico in the Abruzzo, a large, quick-tempered young man who followed his father into soldiering. He gambled away his money and even his shirt. In 1575, working as a labourer at a Capuchin friary in Manfredonia, he was moved by a friar’s words and resolved to change his life. He tried to become a Capuchin but an ulcer on his leg, which troubled him all his life, kept him out. He went instead to the hospital of San Giacomo in Rome as a patient and then as a nurse, and rose to run it. Appalled by the neglect of the sick, he gathered men who would care for them as a mother cares for her only child. With Saint Philip Neri as his confessor he was ordained in 1584. His congregation nursed the plague-stricken and served on the battlefield. He died in Rome in 1614.
prayerTo: Saint Camillus, you knew weakness and sin and you found Christ in the sick. Pray for the sick and dying, for nurses, doctors and carers, and for hospitals. Give me a heart that serves the suffering as a mother serves her only child, and that does not give up on itself. Amen.
penance: Visit someone who is sick or lonely, or do a practical service for a carer who is worn out. If you have a habit you cannot break, offer it to God today.
meditation: He told his brothers to put more heart into their hands. Where could you put more heart into what your hands do?
